title: Zodiac balloon accident

route.from_name: Aero club park at St. Cloud

summary: French military balloon Zodiac departed St. Cloud at approximately 14:00 carrying five aeronauts including military personnel and civilian pilot Aumont-Thiéville. Carried westward by strong wind toward Fontenay-sous-Bois, the balloon flew very low. At 14:30, aeronauts observed throwing out ballast. The balloon struck a chimney and was thrown violently to its side. The car then collided with a house, crashed into telegraph wires, and was blown toward Villiers-sur-Marne. An explosion was heard and the car fell to ground. Three aeronauts were killed immediately; two others died from injuries shortly thereafter.

factors.evidence: The craft was carried over Paris by a strong westerly wind
The car of the balloon collided with a chimney and was thrown violently on its side; crashed into telegraph wires
An explosion was heard, and the car hurtled to the ground

events.text: Balloon departed Aero club park at St. Cloud with five aboard
M. Luisgnann, a cafe proprietor, observed the aeronauts throwing out ballast while balloon flying very low
The car of the balloon collided with a chimney and was thrown violently on its side
The balloon was blown against the side of a house, crashed into some telegraph wires; a few minutes later an explosion was heard, and the car hurtled to the ground

notes: early 1913 balloon; limited investigation; outcome well documented from newspaper accounts

title: Helgoland Island air disaster
summary: Zeppelin LZ 14 was deployed on naval manoeuvers when it encountered a gale 18 miles from its destination. Cold rain caused the lifting gas to contract, reducing buoyancy. The airship descended into the North Sea and broke in two; 13 occupants drowned while 7 were rescued by motor torpedo boats.
probable_cause: Cold rain caused the lifting gas to contract and lose buoyancy, causing the airship to settle into the North Sea. Adverse weather conditions during manoeuvers prevented safe recovery.

factors.evidence: the airship encountered a gale during manoeuvers
the airship broke in two when it settled in the North Sea

events.text: L-1 departs mainland in bad weather carrying 20 people
Aircraft encounters gale while 18 miles from destination
Cold rain causes lifting gas to contract; airship settles 20 miles north of Helgoland into the North Sea
Control car sinks drowning 13 occupants; 7 rescued by motor torpedo boats

notes: minimal text; historical event; occupant count and fatality count from text read as 13 drowned with 7 rescued from 20 aboard

title: Johannisthal air disaster
summary: The Imperial German Navy's L 2 airship exploded during a test flight near Johannisthal Air Field near Berlin when hydrogen gas being vented was sucked into a forward engine and ignited. All 28 passengers and crew on board were killed, making it a total loss.
probable_cause: Hydrogen gas which was being vented was sucked into the forward engine and ignited, causing the airship to explode and burn.

factors.evidence: Hydrogen gas which was being vented was sucked into the forward engine and ignited
The airship exploded and burned, all 28 on board killed
The burning wreckage fell from 900 feet, leaving only crumpled aluminum and twisted wreckage

events.text: During trial trip above Johannisthal, hydrogen gas being vented was sucked into forward engine
Hydrogen ignited causing the airship to explode and burn suddenly at 900 feet altitude
Airship dropped to the ground; thousands of spectators witnessed the disaster; only one man found alive, Lieut. Baron von Bieul, who was fatally injured

notes: Historical airship accident with limited technical documentation
Report from 1914 Almanac provides accounts of witnesses
